episodes.170963: A south to southwest moving line of showers and thunderstorms generated marine thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.170965: Showers and thunderstorms moved southward across the area, producing wind damage and lightning strikes.
episodes.170980: Multiple areas reported flooding over roadways, along with some material that traveled with it between the afternoon of the 10th and the morning of the 11th, due to heavy rains in multiple areas.
episodes.171386: A warm and moist environment placed between a lee trough across the Midlands and a sea breeze shifting inland favored severe thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds.
episodes.171387: Deep moisture, light winds, and a convergence line of clouds led to conditions favorable for late morning waterspouts and damaging wind gusts across coastal waters.
episodes.171388: Deep moisture drawn from the Gulf of Mexico along with large downdraft convective available potential energy ahead of a cold front approaching from the west led to a line of strong thunderstorms capable of producing damaging winds across southeast South Carolina.
episodes.171557: A weak boundary remained overhead while anomalous amounts of moisture remained in place along with moderate instability. Thunderstorms caused heavy rainfall, and with a slow storm motion this led to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.171725: An upper level trough on the West Coast slowly edged in between a ridge of high pressure to the east of the region. This allowed for monsoon moisture to move into the region along with strong southwest flow. Several days of isolated supercells occurred, bringing heavy rain and large hail to the region.
episodes.171726: An upper level trough on the West Coast slowly edged in between a ridge of high pressure to the east of the region. This allowed for monsoon moisture to move into the region along with strong southwest flow. Several days of isolated supercells occurred, bringing heavy rain, localized flooding, and large hail to the region.
episodes.172011: Scattered thunderstorms brought gusty winds to the coastal waters.
episodes.172094: A stalled cold front residing over the Central Appalachians was the main driver behind flash flooding that occurred between August 10th and 11th. The combination of slow moving and repetitive storms led to heavy downpours through the course of the day, before finally winding down that evening as the front began moving out of the area. 24 hour rainfall amounts reported by local observers and weather stations ranged from 1.5 to 3 inches in most places, with locally higher amounts on the upwards of 5 inches observed across north-central West Virginia.||Numerous roads across the northern half of the state became flooded, primarily during the afternoon when storms were at their strongest. This resulted in a few water rescues as vehicles became submerged by the inundating rainfall. Several homes in Ritchie County became surrounded by water for a period of time as well. The most significant damage transpired in Doddridge County, where the building of the local senior center was shoved five feet off of its foundation due to the deluge of water.
episodes.172117: Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 11th in advance of a cold front crossing the region. An isolated severe thunderstorrm produced damaging winds in Madawaska.
episodes.172216: The upper ridge pattern started to break down enabling an influx of deeper moisture (PWAT 2 inches) from the southwest into the afternoon. Isolated strong to severe storms developed where sea breezes and outflows merged near and east of the I-95 corridor, then storms moved offshore of the Atlantic coast.
episodes.172217: The upper ridge pattern started to break down enabling an influx of deeper moisture (PWAT 2 inches) from the southwest into the afternoon. Isolated strong to severe storms developed where sea breezes and outflows merged near and east of the I-95 corridor, then storms moved offshore of the Atlantic coast.
episodes.172426: A cold front slowly progressed east of the Ohio River on August 11th after an active afternoon and evening the day before. Local runoff in Meigs County spilled into the Shade River near Chester just after midnight on the 11th and caused the river to come out of its banks for a brief period of time.
episodes.172923: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots across portions of the coastal waters.
episodes.173139: A surge of monsoon moisture along with an approaching upper level trough created an ideal environment for supercell thunderstorms across Clearwater and Idaho County.
episodes.173284: Above normal precipitable water values, high surface dewpoints, and light southerly or southeasterly steering flow will continued across northern Arizona.  The morning  sounding showed moderate instability, with potential for back-building and/or training. The Weather Prediction Center put northern Arizona in the slight risk categories and a Flash Flood Watch was issued for much of the CWA.
episodes.173291: From August 11-14, thunderstorms produced gusty winds and localized flooding.
episodes.173304: Under an easterly wind flow, subtle disturbances in the upper-levels moved across the state, helping to instigate thunderstorm activity across portions of south-central and southwestern Arizona during the late afternoon and early evening hours. The strongest thunderstorm activity was concentrated from western Maricopa County through most of La Paz and Yuma Counties. Strong instability (SB CAPE of 2000+ J/KG) and high moisture content (PWAT 1.8+ inches) resulted in an environment favorable for the development of strong to severe thunderstorms, which led to instances of damaging wind gusts as well as flash flooding.
episodes.173306: Under deep-layer easterly wind flow, subtle disturbances in the upper-levels helped to instigate thunderstorm activity across portions of south-central and southwestern Arizona during the late afternoon and early evening hours, which then made its way across the Lower Colorado River Valley to affect the town of Winterhaven in extreme Southeast Imperial County. The town was hit with damaging winds in form of dozens of downed power poles, leading to several hundred customers losing power.
episodes.173325: The Sublette County Emergency Manager reported quarter size hail that fell northwest of Daniel, WY.
episodes.173328: A weak upper trough drifted south into East Texas and North Louisiana on August 10th, and provided enough large scale forcing for scattered showers and thunderstorms during peak heating. Available moisture interacting with afternoon temperatures climbing to near 100 degrees resulted in a very unstable air mass, such that an isolated severe thunderstorm developed over the city of Troup in Southern Smith County, producing damaging winds which damaged a metal roof on a building.
episodes.173412: There was continuing rainy pattern that had been in place for a week or more. As daytime heating commenced, thunderstorms began to develop within the moisture rich atmosphere. One of those storms spread northward towards the Baton Rouge Metro and began to train over the area. A notoriously poor drainage underpass was overcome by the heavy rain and became impassable.
episodes.173502: A boundary moving across the state allowed for a cluster of thunderstorms to develop north of the Minnesota Iowa border in the morning and continue south southeast into Iowa through the afternoon. The overall convective parameter was not the most conducive to severe criteria thanks mostly to fairly weak forcing, however as the storms approached Zearing, Iowa the ingredients came together just right. The storm quickly strengthened, resulting in golf ball sized wind driven hail. This caused significant roof, siding, and tree damage in a swath through town.
episodes.173520: Deep lower and mid level moisture remained trapped under an upper high centered over the Rockies.  A weak disturbance moving through northeast flow triggered slow moving storms over the Sacramento Mountains and brought flash flooding to the Soldier Canyon burn scar.
episodes.173521: Deep lower and mid level moisture remained trapped under an upper high centered over the Rockies. A weak disturbance moving through northeast flow triggered slow moving storms across Hudspeth county with flash flooding reported near Cornudas.
episodes.173574: A series of thunderstorms developed along the Northern  Blue Mountain Foothills in Oregon in the late afternoon and evening on Aug. 10th. The storms strengthened as they approached the state border with Washington, resulting in a few of the storms producing damaging winds as they passed over Milton-Freewater, OR. The strongest winds were estimated at 90mph, while damage to several homes, trees, and crops were observed during a storm damage survey.
episodes.173575: A severe thunderstorm that developed in southern Union county went on to impact the towns of La Grande and Wallowa in the afternoon on the 11th. Through the life cycle of the storm, it had produced hailstones to the size of 2.5 inches, while also producing winds up to 60mph. Hailstones produced by the storm caused damage to the sidings and windows of homes as well as produced dents in uncovered cars.
episodes.173594: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms developed along a slow moving cold front across the central Piedmont of central North Carolina. A few of the storms became strong to severe and produced damaging wind gusts and flash flooding across Wake County.
episodes.173618: Thunderstorms moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. One storm produced flash flooding in downstream of the Bighorn burn scar in Finger Rock Canyon.
episodes.173701: As the slow moving Low continued through the region, another round of thunderstorms over the Eastern Washington produced large hail and strong winds to the region. The storms impacted extreme Eastern WA and the North ID Panhandle. Thunderstorms developed along an axis of instability stretching along the border between WA and ID.
episodes.173702: As the slow moving Low continued through the region, another round of thunderstorms over the Eastern Washington produced large hail and strong winds to the region. The storms impacted extreme Eastern WA and ID Panhandle. Thunderstorms developed along an axis of instability stretching along the border between WA and ID.
episodes.173779: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a frontal boundary produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay and Virginia Coastal Waters.
episodes.173793: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Several storms produced flash flooding.
episodes.173795: Moist southeast flow fueled thunderstorms over southern Nevada. Several storms produced severe weather, and a few produced flash flooding.

events.narrative: Wind gust was measured at the Eagle Point NOS/COOPS site.

A 1.5 to 2 mile stretch of road was closed in Lamoille Canyon after a couple of debris flows occurred depositing fine sand, mud, and stones on the roadway. The road was closed for 3 hours for cleanup. The BURN2 RAWS station placed last summer near the Thomas Canyon Campground in Lamoille Canyon measured 0.57 inches of rain in 1 hour, from 15:45 LT to 16:45 LT. At 17:42LT a shift log entry referenced a phone call from a Forest Service representative that said there were some debris flows and that the road was closed. It was reopened at 20:45LT after crews cleared the road.

The MIC at the Elko office reported that 1 to 2 miles east of the South Fork Reservoir, a wash on the east side of the lake filled and overflowed. It was also noted that the overflowing water picked up some debris or had some mixed in it. The water overflowed onto the road for a few inches of depth. Additionally, it was noted that the road that goes around the lake has a steep cliff, and mud and dirt came down the cliff onto the road. This occurred inside a Flood Advisory that was in effect for the area.

The Doddridge County Senior Center in West Union observed substantial damage to its foundation due to the inundation of rain. The wall inside of the building was caved in from downed trees and water rushed down the hill into the basement. Neighborhoods within West Union also suffered basement and roof damage. Minor road damage was observed within the town due to blocked culverts and small landslides.

A downburst occurred from a strong thunderstorm that affected several unoccupied, parked mobile homes. One of the mobile homes was lifted 30 feet into a neighboring mobile home, destroying the lifted mobile home. Other mobile homes suffered some roof and other structural damage, as evidenced from broken glass and insulation around the site.
A large metal building suffered roof damage as a result of a microburst from a collapsing thunderstorm.
Charleston Blvd was flooded one to one and a half feet deep near Jones.

The Shade River near Chester rose above its 17 foot bankfull level during the early morning hours of August 11th. The river crested at 18.45 feet just before dawn and then returned to its banks just after noon that day. High water spilled onto Sugar Run Creek Bridge and Shade River Bridge while the river was out of its banks, which also resulted in minor flooding of low lying areas adjacent to the river.
